Claim_Text: In the 2005 calm-market benchmark window, observed CEFI (0.2023, q*=1) is statistically consistent with matched surrogate nulls (p_dc_Holm = 0.4118, p_static_Holm = 0.3480).

During the 2008 GFC peak, CEFI (0.3656, q*=1) approaches nominal significance against static correlation (p_raw=0.0587) and cross-lag isolation (p_raw=0.0572), with excess over isolation (+0.0778 nats) doubling calm benchmark (+0.0370 nats).
During the 2020 COVID shock (2020-03-23), CEFI (0.3342, q*=2) nominally exceeds static correlation modes (p_raw = 0.0182, z = +2.40).
Across the full 1992-2026 sample, 98.94% of rolling windows exhibit low causal effective dimension (q* <= 4, modal q*=1, 87.7% q* <= 2).

CEFI was higher during liquidity dislocations than valuation repricing (Delta Beta = +0.105, Wald t = 2.40, p = 0.0165 at L=40); contrast remains positive omitting GFC, COVID, or 2022, but sensitive to Dot-Com omission.
A_M = W A W_prime is the transition operator of the constructed interventional macro channel under canonical lifting, with open observational closure (r_closure in [0.39, 0.48] > 0).
Stiefel CEFI achieves high concordance with analytical SVD emergence of Liu et al. 2025 (Pearson rho = 0.819, Spearman rho = 0.821, 87.7% within +/-1 dimension, 63.2% exact match).
Replicating on 49 industry portfolios confirms low dimensionality (modal dimension q*=1, 97.13% q*<=4, mean CEFI = 0.3592).
